Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

conflict noun

disagreement, strife between people

also discord, strife, dissension, clash (of views), conflict of opinion, come into conflict, be in conflict

classical

Sall. Jug. 10.6
Cic. Lael. 24 (Lewis & Short)

discordia, discordiae f.

noun, first declension

discord, strife between people

Strife between people who ought to agree: in a family, among friends, among citizens; the opposite of concordia. Common in the plural, “quarrels” (Cic. Off. 1.86).

Other words

  • dissēnsiō, dissēnsiōnis f. — disagreement, a difference of opinion

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.87: sine acerbitāte (Lewis & Short); Caes. B.C. 1.67.3: dissēnsiō cīvīlis

    A conflict of views, which need not be bitter: Cicero allows a dissēnsiō between friends sine acerbitāte (Off. 1.87). Dissēnsiō cīvīlis is civil strife.

  • contentiō, contentiōnis f. — a struggle, a heated dispute

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 45 (Lewis & Short)

    Properly a straining or exertion (of the voice, of the mind); then a struggle for something, a rivalry, a heated dispute. It also means a comparison. Use it of a conflict that is fought out, in words or for a prize.

  • certāmen, certāminis n. — a contest, a struggle

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.62 (Lewis & Short)

    Any contest, friendly or hostile: a race, a game, a fight. Of a conflict only where something is to be won.

Examples

  • Discordiās in hāc domō nōlō.

    I won’t have quarrelling in this house.composed

See also argument, war, battle, opposite.

SourcesLewis & Short: discordia · Lewis & Short: dissensio · Lewis & Short: contentio · Lewis & Short: certamen

Sallust, Bellum Jugurthīnum 10.6, in the edition’s spelling maxumae.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
